mainTopic: Cleanliness before holy acts (urine, excrement and קריאת שמע, washing at a meal) and the משנה of the immersion before עבודה
overview: This amud first finishes explaining why someone who urinates must wash: there is a מצוה to wipe away the drops, so the hand gets dirty. The גמרא says this supports רבי אמי, who forbids going out with urine drops on one's legs because people may suspect a defect and spread rumors that his children are ממזרים. רב פפא then rules that excrement 'in its place' forbids קריאת שמע. The גמרא explains that he means excrement that shows when sitting but not when standing, and that this case is filthier than the excrement on the body that רב הונא and רב חסדא argue about. A ברייתא then teaches how to wash hands at a meal after going out to urinate, and that one washes inside to avoid חשד. רב חסדא and רב נחמן בר יצחק limit that rule. A new משנה follows: no one enters the עזרה for עבודה without טבילה, even if he is טהור, and the כהן גדול does five טבילות and ten קידושין on יום כיפור. בן זומא explains the first immersion with a קל וחומר about entering holiness. רבי יהודה says it is a reminder of forgotten טומאה. The גמרא asks what practical difference lies between them, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Wiping urine drops supports רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The reason someone who urinates must wash is that there is a מצוה to wipe off the drops. The גמרא says this supports רבי אמי, who forbids going out with urine drops on one's legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a מצוה to wipe off the drops. This supports רבי אמי, who said: A person may not go out with drops of urine on his legs, because he looks like someone whose organ is cut. People will then spread a rumor that his children are ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The words 'מצוה לשפשף' finish the explanation of why urinating requires washing: you wipe the drops with your hand, so your hand needs washing. The גמרא then points out that this idea supports a ruling of רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man with a כרות שפכה cannot father children. If drops of urine are seen on a man's legs, people might think he has this defect and assume his children belong to someone else. That is why רבי אמי forbids going out like this, and why wiping the drops is a real מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: this supports him (a proof for someone's view)
a man whose organ is cut and who cannot father children
children born from a forbidden relationship

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'מצוה לשפשף' are not a new topic. They are the last words of the explanation that began on the previous amud, about why urinating requires washing hands and feet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that wiping urine drops is not just about cleanliness. It also protects a person's family from harmful rumors.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה to wipe off the drops.
phrases.notes: End of the explanation of why urinating requires washing: the hand that wipes becomes dirty.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Ami,
for Rabbi Ami said:
It is forbidden for a person to go out
with drops of urine on his legs,
because he looks like one whose organ is cut,
and he causes a rumor about his children
that they are mamzerim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reason for washing after urinating (on the previous amud) and links it to רבי אמי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's rule that one may not go out with urine drops on his legs
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement that there is a מצוה to wipe off urine drops

steps.title: רב פפא: excrement in its place forbids שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a person with excrement at its place of exit may not recite קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If there is excrement in its place, it is forbidden to recite שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we are discussing bodily cleanliness, the גמרא brings a new rule from רב פפא about excrement and קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In its place' means at the body's opening, not somewhere else on the skin. The rule is short and unclear, and the גמרא will now ask exactly what case it means.

keyTerms.meaning: in its place (at the body's opening)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Excrement in its place,
it is forbidden to recite Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related topic of bodily cleanliness, brought because of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Excrement at its place of exit forbids reciting קריאת שמע.

steps.title: What case does רב פפא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a dilemma. If the excrement is visible, the rule is obvious. If it is not visible, the rule is impossible, because no one's body is perfectly clean inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it can be seen, that is obvious. If it cannot be seen, the Torah was not given to the ministering angels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's rule with an either/or question: either way, the rule seems useless or unreasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the excrement can be seen, it is just like dirt on the body, so why do we need רב פפא to tell us? If it is hidden inside the body, everyone has that, and the Torah does not demand that people be as pure as angels.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the circumstances?
the Torah was not given to angels; it does not demand the impossible

phrases.english: What is the case?
If it is visible, it is obvious.
If it is not visible,
the Torah was not given to the ministering angels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's rule by showing it has no sensible case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling about excrement in its place
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dilemma: a visible case is obvious, and an invisible case would demand an impossible standard.

steps.title: Visible when sitting, hidden when standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב פפא means a middle case: the excrement shows when the person sits but is hidden when he stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for this case: when he sits it can be seen, and when he stands it cannot be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma by finding a middle case that is neither obvious nor impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is not fully visible, we might have thought it is allowed. Since it is not deep inside, it is not an impossible standard. רב פפא teaches that even this partly hidden case forbids קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where when sitting it is visible,
and when standing it is not visible.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule has no real case: it is either obvious or impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies when the excrement is visible only while sitting.

steps.title: How is this different from excrement on the body?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא forbids קריאת שמע so simply, when there is a מחלוקת between רב הונא and רב חסדא about excrement on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from excrement on one's flesh? For it was said: If there is excrement on his flesh, or his hands were in the bathroom, רב הונא said it is permitted to recite שמע, and רב חסדא said it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא again. Excrement on the skin is disputed, so how can רב פפא state a clear prohibition for a case that is even less visible?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, even visible excrement on the skin does not stop קריאת שמע. So why should excrement that is only sometimes visible forbid it? רב פפא's rule seems to go against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was stated (an אמוראים dispute)

phrases.english: And how is this different from excrement on his flesh?
As it was stated:
Excrement on his flesh,
or his hands were in the bathroom,
Rav Huna said:
It is permitted to recite Shema,
and Rav Chisda said:
It is forbidden to recite Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב פפא after his case was defined in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Excrement on the skin is disputed, and רב הונא permits it, so a less visible case should not be a clear prohibition.

steps.title: In its place the filth is much greater
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that excrement in its place is much filthier than excrement elsewhere on the body, so even רב הונא would forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In its place, the filth is great. Not in its place, the filth is not great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At its place of exit the excrement is fresh and smells strongly. Once it is elsewhere on the body it has dried and is less foul. So the מחלוקת of רב הונא and רב חסדא is only about the milder case, and everyone agrees with רב פפא.
steps.whatToRemember: Excrement visible only when sitting forbids קריאת שמע according to everyone, because fresh excrement in its place is much filthier. The מחלוקת of רב הונא and רב חסדא is only about excrement elsewhere on the body.

phrases.english: In its place, the filth is great;
not in its place, the filth is not great.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's rule seems to go against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Excrement in its place is more severe, so everyone forbids קריאת שמע there.

steps.title: Washing at a meal after urinating
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who leaves a meal to urinate washes one hand when he returns. If he stopped to talk for a long time, he washes both hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught a הלכה about a meal: A person goes out to urinate; he washes one hand and comes back in. If he talked with his friend and stayed a long time, he washes both hands and comes back in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about washing hands at a meal after urinating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One hand is enough because only the hand he used to wipe the drops got dirty. If he talked for a long time, he stopped paying attention to keeping his hands clean, so both hands need washing.

keyTerms.meaning: and stayed away a long time

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught a halacha about a meal:
A person goes out to urinate,
he washes one hand and comes back in.
If he talked with his friend and stayed a long time,
he washes both hands and comes back in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of washing after urinating from step 1, now applied to a meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After urinating, wash one hand. After a long break, wash both hands.

steps.title: Wash inside to avoid suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: wash your hands inside at your seat, not outside, so the other guests do not suspect you did not wash, and pass the water jug around.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he washes, he should not wash outside and then come in, because of suspicion. Rather, he comes in, sits in his place, washes both hands, and passes the jug around to the guests.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds how and where to wash, so that no one suspects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he washes outside, the guests did not see it and may think he did not wash. Washing at his seat and offering the jug to the others makes it clear to everyone that he washed.
steps.whatToRemember: After urinating at a meal: one hand normally, both hands after a long break. Always wash inside at your seat in front of the guests to avoid חשד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches the principle of avoiding חשד: a person must act in a way that others can see is proper, and not only be proper in private.

phrases.english: And when he washes,
he should not wash outside and then come in,
because of suspicion.
Rather, he comes in and sits in his place
and washes both hands,
and passes the jug around to the guests.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל, לֹא יִטּוֹל מִבַּחוּץ וְיִכָּנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with how and where to wash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wash at your seat in front of the guests, not outside, to avoid suspicion.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the washing-inside rule to drinking
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the rule to wash inside in front of everyone only applies when you come back to drink. If you come back to eat, you may wash outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We only said this about someone coming back to drink. But if he comes back to eat, he washes outside and comes in, because everyone knows he is fussy about cleanliness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a limit to the ברייתא from the last step about washing inside so nobody suspects you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that guests might think you didn't wash. For eating, nobody would suspect that, because people are naturally fussy about touching food with dirty hands. So the worry only applies to drinking, where you might skip washing.

keyTerms.meaning: he is fastidious / fussy about cleanliness

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
We only said this for drinking,
but to eat —
he washes outside and enters,
because it is well known that he is fastidious.
phrases.notes: No one eats food with dirty hands, so there is no suspicion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's rule of washing inside to the case of drinking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing inside in front of the guests is only needed when returning to drink. When returning to eat, one may wash outside.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: for me, even drinking is fine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he can wash outside even when coming back to drink, because everyone knows how fussy he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: And I, even when coming back to drink, may wash outside. People know that I am fastidious.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that for a person known to be very careful, like himself, the worry doesn't exist even for drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about what others will suspect. If people already know you are very careful, there is nothing to suspect. So the reason behind רב חסדא's limit stretches further for such a person.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole washing-inside rule is about suspicion (חשד). Where there is no suspicion, because of eating or because of a known careful person, you may wash outside.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And I, even to drink as well,
they know that I am fastidious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב חסדא's logic to a personal case: a known careful person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person known to be fastidious may wash outside even when returning only to drink.

steps.title: משנה: no one enters the courtyard for service without immersing
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that anyone entering the עזרה to do עבודה must first do טבילה, even if he is already טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may not enter the Temple courtyard for the service, even if he is pure, until he immerses.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a basic rule: immersion is required before entering the עזרה for עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprising part is the word 'even pure'. Normally טבילה removes טומאה. Here, someone who has no טומאה still has to immerse. That is why the גמרא will soon ask what this immersion is for.
steps.confusionAlert: This immersion is NOT for removing impurity, since the person is already pure. Don't read it as a normal purification immersion.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A person does not enter the courtyard for the service
even if he is pure, until he immerses.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין אָדָם נִכְנָס לָעֲזָרָה לַעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: a new משנה about the immersion before עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone entering the עזרה for עבודה must immerse first, even if he is pure.

steps.title: משנה: the High Priest's five immersions and ten washings
steps.stepSummary: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול does five טבילות and ten קידושי ידים ורגלים. All of them happen in the holy area on בית הפרוה, except the first one. A linen sheet is spread for modesty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול immerses five times and sanctifies his hands and feet ten times on that day. All of them are in the holy area, on the roof of בית הפרוה, except for this first one alone. They spread a sheet of fine linen between him and the people, and he sanctified his hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It describes the special immersions of the כהן גדול on יום כיפור and where they take place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול immerses each time he changes clothes between gold and white garments. Each immersion has a washing of hands and feet before it and after it, which makes ten. The first immersion is the general one every כהן does, so it may be done outside the holy area. The other four are special to יום כיפור and must be done inside.

keyTerms.meaning: sanctifications: washing hands and feet from the כיור
the Parva chamber in the Temple

phrases.english: Five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day,
and all of them are in the holy area, on the Parva chamber,
except for this one alone.
phrases.notes: The first immersion, mentioned at the start of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: פֵּרְסוּ סָדִין שֶׁל בּוּץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָעָם
phrases.english: They spread a sheet of fine linen between him and the people
(he sanctified his hands and feet).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from the general rule to the כהן גדול's day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול does five immersions and ten sanctifications on יום כיפור. All are in the holy area except the first.

steps.title: בן זומא is asked: why this immersion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a question put to בן זומא: why is the immersion from the משנה's first line needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked בן זומא: This immersion, why is it needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first immersion. This sets up בן זומא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the person is already pure, the immersion cannot be about removing טומאה. So what is its purpose? The question is sincere. It seeks a reason, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא famous for sharp reasoning

phrases.english: GEMARA:
They asked Ben Zoma:
This immersion, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason for requiring a pure person to immerse before entering the עזרה?

steps.title: בן זומא's קל וחומר from the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא answers with a קל וחומר. The כהן גדול must immerse when moving from one holy place to another. Surely someone moving from a regular place into a holy place must immerse too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Just as one who moves from holy to holy, from a place where entering impure is punished with כרת to another such place, requires immersion, then one who moves from non-holy to holy, from a place with no כרת to a place with כרת, surely he should require immersion!
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא answers the question with a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול immerses even though he only moves between two holy areas. Entering the עזרה from outside is a bigger jump: from חול to קודש, from no כרת to כרת. So it should certainly need immersion. This shows the immersion is about entering holiness, not about purity.

keyTerms.meaning: spiritual cutting off, the punishment for entering impure

steps.whyThisMatters: It defines this immersion as a holiness immersion, connected to the act of entering a higher level of קדושה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Just as one who moves from holy to holy,
and from a place punishable by karet
to a place punishable by karet, requires immersion,
one who moves from non-holy to holy,
and from a place not punishable by karet
to a place punishable by karet,
is it not logical that he requires immersion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's question using the כהן גדול's immersions from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The immersion is learned by קל וחומר from the כהן גדול's immersions between holy areas. Moving from חול to קודש is a greater change, so it surely needs immersion.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: an immersion to jog the memory
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives a different reason. This is a סרך טבילה, an extra immersion, meant to make a person remember any old טומאה he has and stay away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: This is an extra, supplementary immersion. It is so that he will remember any old impurity he has and hold back from the service.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה offers a second, different reason for the same immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בן זומא, the immersion is about holiness. For רבי יהודה, it is a safeguard. While preparing to immerse, a person may suddenly remember that he became טמא earlier. Then he will not enter.

keyTerms.meaning: an old impurity he forgot about
and he will withdraw or stay away

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the pre-עבודה immersion. בן זומא says it is for holiness, by קל וחומר. רבי יהודה says it is a reminder of forgotten טומאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
This is a supplementary immersion,
so that he will remember an old impurity he has
and withdraw.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סֶרֶךְ טְבִילָה הִיא זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason from בן זומא's for the same immersion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The immersion is a reminder: it makes a person recall forgotten טומאה so he will not enter the עזרה.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real disagreement is between בן זומא and רבי יהודה about the reason for the immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where בן זומא's reason and רבי יהודה's reason would lead to a different law. This is a setup line, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them agree that a person must immerse before entering the עזרה. They only disagree about why. So the גמרא wants to find a case where the reason makes a difference in practice. For בן זומא it is a real requirement learned from a קל וחומר, and for רבי יהודה it is an extra reminder immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree; asks for the practical difference between two opinions

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that one of them holds the immersion is not needed. Both agree you must immerse. The question is only about the reason, and what result that reason causes.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" refers to בן זומא and רבי יהודה from steps 14 and 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the two different answers in steps 14 and 15 and asks for the practical difference between them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do the reasons of בן זומא (a קל וחומר) and רבי יהודה (a סרך טבילה) lead to different laws?
